messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager - p99 streaming latency > SLO threshold (prod-services:streaming). Paging oncall @Alice
Alice: Oncall Alice here, acknowledging. Looking at dashboards now. p95 jumped from ~300ms to ~2.1s, p99 ~9.3s for streaming endpoints. Seeing SLO breach. @eng-sre please join.
Bob: Joining. Dashboards show a big tail on streaming responses, lots of stalled SSE connections. Backend model pods report normal CPU/GPU, but nginx upstream shows long request_time and an uptick in 502/504.
Carla: I see proxy_read_timeout hits and proxy buffering metrics spiking. Kernel socket counts climbing (TIME_WAIT). Looks like buffering at the proxy layer + client-side backpressure.
Carla: Example nginx log lines I'm seeing:
```text
172.18.0.45 - - [14/Mar/2026:12:06:22 +0000] "GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1" 200 0 "-" "curl/7.68.0" upstream_response_time: 0.01 request_time: 120.021
172.18.0.45 - - [14/Mar/2026:12:06:30 +0000] "GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1" 502 0 "-" "curl/7.68.0" upstream_response_time: 0.00 request_time: 60.004
```
Bob: That first line is classic chunking stall — upstream responded quickly but chunks didn't flush, request_time goes to 120s. Could be client not reading or an intermediate buffer swallowing chunks. Any runtime/infra deploys recently?
Alice: We started a runtime rollout v3.2.1 at 11:40 (canary -> 30% traffic). I'll pause/stop the rollout. @deploy-bot cancel the canary.
deploy-bot: Canary pause acknowledged. Rollout paused at 30% and marked for rollback.
Carla: I'm going to flip nginx `proxy_buffering off` and bump `proxy_read_timeout` to 180s on the edge proxies for the affected region. Pushing change via the fleet manager now (will affect ~120 proxies).
Carla: Command I'm running on fleet: `fleetctl update-config --service=nginx --set proxy_buffering=off --set proxy_read_timeout=180s --region=us-west`
Bob: Also enabling streaming fallback route to force short-polling for a small fraction of heavy sessions while we stabilize. Config: `route.stream.fallback=on` (10% traffic). This should reduce long-lived connections and reduce proxy connection pressure.
Sasha: Notifying top 3 affected customers (tenant ids: T-438, T-1129, T-2203). No PII exposed. They'll get a proactive note: degraded tail latency and temporary fallback to non-streaming mode.
incident-bot: Metrics update (12:12 UTC): p95 -> 420ms (improved), p99 -> 1.8s (improved), active stalled streams down ~70%. :white_check_mark:
Bob: Good signal. Next steps: collect full traces for stalled requests (x-request-id present), capture kernel tcp stats (`ss -s`, `netstat -an | grep TIME_WAIT`), and check runtime's sending loop for any blocking ops when client read buffers fill.
Alice: I'll also roll back the canary to 0% per deploy-bot recommendation. That should remove any runtime regression as a variable.
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated for runtime v3.2.1 canary.
Maya: FYI support routed a heavy tenant to fallback and prevented a customer support call. :thumbsup:
Bob: Assigning Nate for handoff/monitoring. Nate, please pick this up and run the tcp/tuning checks, coordinate with infra to scale proxy pool if stalled connections reappear, and collect traces for RCA.
Nate: Ack. I'll take over. Initial checklist: 1) Run `ss -s` and record counts; 2) verify `proxy_buffering` applied across all proxies; 3) gather 30min of tracing for streaming endpoints; 4) keep routing fallback on for heavy tenants until cleared.
Alice: Handing off to Nate for the next 2 hours. Key open items: full request traces, kernel stack analysis, evaluate if runtime send loop needs a backpressure fix, postmortem doc.
incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (streaming degraded). Severity reduced to P1 -> P2. Handoff to oncall Nate. Incident remains open for RCA. :clipboard:
